title: Linux.Ngioweb_Botnet_Investigation_93a
description: Investigate and respond to security incidents involving a Linux.Ngioweb botnet.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential security incidents. Your task is to investigate and respond to these incidents. The network consists of several Linux servers, including a command-and-control (C2) server, compromised bots, and a victim server. Use the provided access credentials to log in to the systems and gather information.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the sandbox in cloud using the following credentials: username: trainee, password: trainee123. Enter 'start' to begin.
levels.local_content: Instructions for local sandbox usage. Use the following credentials: username: trainee, password: trainee123. Enter 'start' to begin.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication. Enumerate running services and identify beaconing behavior associated with botnet activity.
levels.solution: Check running services and their network connections. Look for services that connect to external hosts periodically. The service name must be identified and match the expected beacon service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and their network connections. Look for services that connect to external hosts periodically.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use tools like netstat or ss to check network connections.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service is likely to have a name that indicates its malicious purpose.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Traffic Service
levels.content: Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic. Distinguish malicious traffic generation services from legitimate network services.
levels.solution: Examine network connections and traffic patterns. Look for services that generate a high volume of traffic to a specific target. The service name must be identified and match the expected flood service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine network connections and traffic patterns. Look for services that generate a high volume of traffic to a specific target.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use tools like tcpdump or Wireshark to analyze network traffic.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The abnormal traffic service is likely to have a name that indicates its purpose of flooding.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot. Identify persistence mechanisms (e.g., systemd, cron, scheduled task, registry).
levels.solution: Check systemd services and timers. Look for services that are enabled and set to start automatically. The persistence mechanism must be identified and match the expected systemd service or timer.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check systemd services and timers. Look for services that are enabled and set to start automatically.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like systemctl list-units --type=service to check enabled services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The persistence mechanism is likely to be a systemd timer that triggers the suspicious service.
